newsitem.title: USA: Bankers Trust profits up 20 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust profits up 20 percent.

text.p: Bankers Trust New York Corp. said Wednesday strong revenue growth and a higher return on equity pushed its profits up 20 percent in the second quarter.

The company -- which owns Bankers Trust, the seventh biggest bank in the country -- said its net income for the three months ended June 30 climbed to $181 million, or $2.07 a share, from $151 million, or $1.67 a share, a year ago.
The New York-based firm, which plans to acquire the Alex. Brown brokerage this year, said its total revenues expanded by more than 23 percent to $1.29 billion from $1.04 billion.
Return on common equity in the quarter improved to 15.2 percent from 12.9 percent a year ago.
"Broad-based revenue gains in Bankers Trust's global businesses continued to drive an improvement in profitability in the second quarter," Chairman Frank Newman said in a statement.
"Compared to last year, revenue growth was especially strong in our trading and sales, investment banking and risk management services business units."

The company said a rebound in risk management services and strong performances in nearly all other businesses helped push up its trading revenue and trading-related net interest revenue by $220 million.
It added that increases in private placement, merger and acquisition and loan syndication activities helped increase corporate finance fees by $38 million.
The company said total non-interest expenses for the quarter increased by $203 million, or 25 percent, with personnel-related expenses contributing $172 million to the increase.

It said salaries rose by 15 percent to $232 million due to growth in the number of employees and annual pay increases while incentive compensation and employee benefits jumped by 60 percent to $377 million, primarily as a result of higher levels of revenues and profits.
The employee-related costs amounted to about 47.4 percent of total revenues, which had been expected due to the competitive pressures in the industry.
The company said its already strong credit quality continued to improve during the quarter, with cash-basis loans declining to $305 million from $573 million a year ago.
It also said it continued to carry no provision for credit losses.
Bankers Trust stock added 62.5 cents to $94.875 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
